newsitem.title: UK: Ofwat welcomes Anglian's Hartlepool price cut.
newsitem.headline: Ofwat welcomes Anglian's Hartlepool price cut.

text.p: British water industry regulator Ofwat said on Wednesday that lower price limits pledged for Hartlepool Water customers in its takeover by Anglian was "good news."

In a statement on the planned 19.5 million pound takeover, Ofwat head Ian Byatt said Anglian's licence would be extended to include Hartlepool Water's area although the latter would retain its separate identity.

Anglian will pay 266 pence per share with a loan note alternative for Hartlepool and said it would cut prices for customers in the area by five percent from April 1, when the joint licence comes into force.
Ofwat also welcomed Anglian's offer of free optional meter installation packages and the merger's introduction of competition in the north east of England.
Byatt said he would continue to receive separate information on Hartlepool to mitigate against the loss of a comparison among water companies.
"Compared with the loss from a water and sewerage company merger, the detriment in this case is modest and the remedy I have sought recognises this fact," he added.

As the planned merger concerns assets of under 30 million stg, it is too small to come under regulations which call for a bid of that size or above to be referred automatically to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
